# Executive summary

Choosing an R tutorial often means inspecting its repository to check the requirements and find evidence that the exercises still work. Lessons use different formats and describe their requirements inconsistently. Instructors and learners may also struggle to determine whether anyone still maintains them.

**tutorialverse will help instructors and learners find R tutorials suited to their needs, understand the prerequisites, and see when the materials were last checked and reviewed.** We will build an R package that checks tutorials through adapters for existing engines and records the results in a common format. A searchable registry will bring those reports together with tutorial descriptions and human reviews. Authors will keep their lessons in their own repositories, with a community process for reviewing submissions and handling outdated entries.

The 12-month project will initially support learnr, learnr2, and Quarto Live, with four small example tutorials to test the adapters across teaching contexts. Carpentries-style materials will also be indexed, with stated limits on automated checks. Existing tools will provide browser execution and static hosting.
